subject: Human Evolution
title: Ardi's Grasping Toe
description: A 60-second lesson on Ardi's Grasping Toe.

hook.text: Ardi walked upright 4.4 million years ago, yet her big toe stuck out sideways like a thumb—for gripping.

buildup.text: Modern human big toes are aligned straight, providing a push-off platform for efficient walking.

discovery.text: Ardi's opposable toe means she was bipedal on the ground but still an effective tree climber.

twist.text: This mix challenges a clean narrative: bipedalism wasn't an instant switch but a gradual transition.

climax.text: It took over 2 million years for the human foot to fully commit to the ground and give up the trees.

punchline.text: One toe tells a two-million-year story.

quiz.question: What was unusual about Ardi's big toe?
options: It was opposable, like a thumb
It was fused to other toes
